caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Ethiopia's debt reflects its state-led investment model. From 79.6% of GDP in 2006 it fell to 30.2% by 2009 as early HIPC relief and growth took hold, then climbed again as the government borrowed heavily, much of it from China, for dams, railways, and industrial parks: 58.2% by 2018. The Tigray war and forex crisis pushed it into distress, and in December 2023 Ethiopia missed a Eurobond coupon, effectively defaulting. The July 2024 IMF program ($3.4 billion) anchored a restructuring under the G20 Common Framework; debt is projected at 43.0% in 2025, down from the 2024 level, as restructuring and the birr float re-denominate the burden. Sustainability now depends on completing the restructuring and sustaining the reform momentum.
inflation_management: Ethiopia's inflation has been chronically high, driven by monetized deficits, a controlled exchange rate, and conflict. It hit 44.4% in 2008, the series high, during the global food crisis, then 33.2% in 2011. A decade of relative stability (6-16%) ended with the Tigray war and forex shortages: inflation rose to 26.8% in 2021, 33.9% in 2022, and 30.2% in 2023. The July 29, 2024 decision to float the birr, under the IMF program, was the regime change: pass-through was sharp but the parallel market premium collapsed, and inflation fell to 21.0% in 2024 and a projected 13.2% in 2025. The central bank is moving toward interest-rate-based policy, but credibility is still being built.

key_events.event: Global food crisis pushed inflation to 44.4%, the series high; GDP in USD terms was just $15.3bn.
Abiy Ahmed became prime minister, launching political and economic reforms.
Tigray war (November 2020 - November 2022 ceasefire) devastated the north and strained finances.
Missed Eurobond coupon in December 2023, entering sovereign default; sought G20 Common Framework treatment.
July 29, 2024: birr floated and IMF approved a $3.4 billion four-year program; inflation began falling from 30%+ levels.
Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam inaugurated; debt restructuring talks with bondholders continued into 2026.

outlook_next_decade: The base case is reform-led stabilization: if the birr stays flexible and the debt restructuring completes, Ethiopia could return to 7%+ growth on its demographic and industrial base. Upside is large (manufacturing, services liberalization); downside is that conflict resumes or reforms stall, in which case inflation and debt distress return quickly. Uncertainty is high: the 2024 package was bold, but implementation risk and regional tensions (notably with Eritrea) are material.
